summary: Parses quoted tokens from input string a1 into output buffers a2 and a3. Nullifies delimiter characters located by sub_587C20, returns -1 on a null or empty input, then when the period separator asc_5C30AC is present copies the first quoted substring into a2 and the following quoted substring into a3. Returns 0 on success.

operations.description: Return -1 immediately when the input string a1 is null.
Initialize the output indices v3 and v18 to 0.
Locate and nullify the delimiter characters in a1 via sub_587C20 using unk_5C30B8, word_5C30B4, and asc_5C30B0; each found position is set to 0.
Return -1 when a1 is empty (strlen == 0 after delimiter nullification).
Zero-initialize the output buffers a2 and a3 when each is non-null.
Find the period separator asc_5C30AC in a1 via sub_587C20; if not found, skip the entire token parse and return 0.
If the first character of a1 equals 34 (the '"' literal), parse the quoted content directly; otherwise scan ahead until a quote character is found.
Copy the quoted content into a2: walk characters starting at the quote (offsets 0x1, 0x2, ...) until the closing quote or the separator position, then null-terminate a2.
After the separator, scan up to a 256-byte window for the next quote and copy the following quoted content into a3, then null-terminate a3.

unresolved: Whether the quote character 34 delimits both tokens or only the first is not established from this packet alone.
The 256-byte window after the separator is an arbitrary bound; its semantic meaning (buffer size vs. scan limit) is unknown.
